label: Healthcare
description: A hospital or health system: emergency department, inpatient units, operating rooms, the EHR and medical devices, a hospital command center under HICS. Plans: the CMS emergency preparedness program (42 CFR 482.15: all-hazards risk assessment, testing twice a year, one exercise of which may be a facilitated tabletop), the HVA, EHR downtime procedures, and HIPAA breach notification (individuals within 60 days of discovery).

vocabulary.frontline: charge nurses, ED physicians, unit clerks, security officers, biomedical technicians, registration staff

it: bed management and patient flow board
ot: PACS access control and infant security
medical devices on the network (pumps, monitors, imaging)

roles.name: Administrator on Call (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the hospital, the HICS activation and the big decisions.

roles.name: Chief Information Security Officer (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the EHR, the network, the devices and the investigation.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns patient and family messaging, social media and the press.

roles.name: Director of Security
roles.description: Owns access control, visitor management and the police liaison.

roles.name: Chief Nursing Officer (Operations Section Chief)
roles.description: Owns patient care, bed capacity, diversion and the units.

roles.name: Chief Privacy Officer (Compliance)
roles.description: Owns the HIPAA breach risk assessment and OCR / state notification timing.

roles.name: Director of Facilities (Infrastructure Branch Director)
roles.description: Owns generators, medical gas, HVAC, water and elevators.

roles.name: Director of Clinical Engineering (Biomed)
roles.description: Owns networked medical devices and their isolation.

outsideParties: CMS and the state department of health
HHS / ASPR and the healthcare coalition
local EMS and the regional trauma system
the blood supplier and pharmacy wholesaler
HHS Office for Civil Rights (HIPAA breach reports)
the cyber insurer and incident response firm

sceneAnchors.public: inside a hospital emergency department waiting area: rows of chairs, families waiting, a registration desk, dark wall-mounted monitors, bright even lighting
sceneAnchors.control: inside a hospital command center: a conference room with a whiteboard, laptops and phones on the table, staff in scrubs and lanyards wearing colored vests
sceneAnchors.exterior: a hospital ambulance bay: two ambulances with doors open, sliding glass doors, paramedics with a stretcher, overcast daylight

noiseExamples: a visitor elevator stuck between floors
a parking garage gate stuck up
a badge printer out of cards
a nurse asking for a password reset
pressureExamples: a family member's Facebook post about a cancelled surgery
a rumor that patient records were leaked
a health reporter asking if the ED is on diversion
the state health department asking for a status report
a surgeon demanding the OR schedule be restored
counsel asking when the 60-day HIPAA notification clock started
